lem-shared-minimum-poisson-count-couplin:
## Statement

Let $h\ge0$ and let $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0$. Let $C,R_1,R_2$ be
independent counts with laws
$$C\sim\operatorname{Pois}(h\min(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)),\quad R_1\sim\operatorname{Pois}(h(\lambda_1-\lambda_2)^+),\quad R_2\sim\operatorname{Pois}(h(\lambda_2-\lambda_1)^+),$$
and set $K_1=C+R_1$, $K_2=C+R_2$. Then $K_i\sim\operatorname{Pois}(h\lambda_i)$,
$$\mathbb E(K_1-K_2)=h(\lambda_1-\lambda_2),\qquad \operatorname{Var}(K_1-K_2)=h|\lambda_1-\lambda_2|,$$
and
$$\operatorname{Cov}(K_1,K_2)=h\min(\lambda_1,\lambda_2).$$
alg-explicit-poisson-tau-leaping:
## Definition

**Inputs.** A finite-channel reaction propensity system
[[def-reaction-network-propensity-system-and-generator]], an initial state
$x_0\in E$, a deterministic grid $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_N=T$ with finite $N$,
and a draw budget $B\in\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$. Write
$h_n=t_{n+1}-t_n$. At each step the count vector has the product law whose
$j$th marginal is $\operatorname{Pois}(a_j(x_n)h_n)$, as defined in
[[def-scalar-poisson-count-law]]. The budget counts scalar Poisson draws.

**Procedure.** Set $x=x_0$, grid index $n=0$, Poisson-draw counter $d=0$, and
status **horizon**.

1. If $n=N$, return the completed path with status **horizon**. If $x\notin E$,
   set status **invalid-state**, hold $x$ fixed to $T$, and return. If
   $\lambda(x)=0$, hold $x$ fixed to $T$ and return status
   **absorbed**.
2. If fewer than $R$ draws remain in budget $B$ (that is, $B-d<R$), return the path prefix with
   status **budget-exhausted**; it does not define a terminal sample at $T$.
3. Draw conditionally independent $K_{j,n}\sim\operatorname{Pois}(a_j(x)h_n)$,
   $1\le j\le R$, and set $y=x+\sum_{j=1}^R K_{j,n}\nu_j$. Increase
   $d\leftarrow d+R$.
4. Advance time to $t_{n+1}$. If $y\notin E$, set $x=y$, set status
   **invalid-state**, and keep $y$ fixed through all remaining grid times. If
   $y\in E$, set $x\leftarrow y$, increment $n\leftarrow n+1$, and continue.

The run has at most $N$ iterations. Each valid step uses exactly $R$ scalar
Poisson draws, $R$ propensity evaluations, and one finite stoichiometric
update. Under the unit-operation convention that each scalar draw,
propensity evaluation, and stoichiometric update costs one unit, its work is
$O(RN)$; the cost internal to a particular random-number generator is
excluded. Under the same convention, an event-count SSA implementation does
one exponential draw and one channel selection per simulated event, so its
work on a realized path is $O(M_T)$, where $M_T$ is that path's event count
before $T$. This compares operation counts only; it does not compare
parameter-dependent random-number costs. The method is approximate; its
Poisson leap can leave the physical state set, and no error guarantee is
asserted here for unbounded rates or the budget-exhausted prefix.
def-density-scaled-jump-and-chemical-lan:
## Definition

Fix finitely many stoichiometric vectors $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_R\in\mathbb Z^d$,
an open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, nonnegative propensity functions
$a_j:U\to[0,\infty)$, and a volume parameter $V\ge1$. At a density state
$x\in U$ for which every positive-rate destination $x+\nu_j/V$ lies in $U$,
the density-scaled jump model has jump $\nu_j/V$ at rate $Va_j(x)$. For a
twice differentiable test function $\phi$ defined at those destinations, its
generator is
$$\mathcal L_V\phi(x)=V\sum_{j:a_j(x)>0} a_j(x)\bigl(\phi(x+\nu_j/V)-\phi(x)\bigr).$$

Put $b(x)=\sum_j\nu_j a_j(x)$ and
$C(x)=\sum_j a_j(x)\nu_j\nu_j^{\mathsf T}$. The associated
**chemical Langevin diffusion generator** is
$$\mathcal G_V\phi(x)=b(x)\cdot\nabla\phi(x) +\frac{1}{2V}\sum_{j=1}^R a_j(x)\, \nu_j^{\mathsf T}D^2\phi(x)\nu_j.$$
A Markov diffusion with this generator is called the chemical Langevin
model here. The definition does not assert existence, uniqueness, positivity,
or approximation accuracy for either process. In an SDE representation the
drift is $b$ and the covariance matrix per unit time is $C/V$.
lem-poisson-tau-leap-moment-and-covarian:
## Statement

Fix a state $x\in E$ and step $h\ge0$ in
[[alg-explicit-poisson-tau-leaping]]. Let
$\Delta Y=\sum_{j=1}^R\nu_jK_j$, where conditionally independent
$K_j\sim\operatorname{Pois}(a_j(x)h)$. Then
$$\mathbb E[\Delta Y\mid x]=h\sum_{j=1}^R a_j(x)\nu_j,$$
$$\operatorname{Cov}(\Delta Y\mid x)=h\sum_{j=1}^R a_j(x)\nu_j\nu_j^{\mathsf T},$$
and
$$\mathbb E[\|\Delta Y\|^2\mid x] =h\sum_{j=1}^R a_j(x)\|\nu_j\|^2 +h^2\left\|\sum_{j=1}^R a_j(x)\nu_j\right\|^2.$$
thm-minimum-intensity-tau-leap-level-var:
## Statement

Assume the finite-state reaction system of
[[def-reaction-network-propensity-system-and-generator]] has propensities
bounded on $E$ and extended by zero to states outside $E$. Let
$h_\ell=T2^{-\ell}$ for $\ell\ge1$, and couple a fine step $h=h_\ell$ to a
coarse step $2h$ as follows. On each of the two half intervals, with fine
state $x$ and coarse state $z$, use for channel $j$ a shared
$\operatorname{Pois}(h\min(a_j(x),a_j(z)))$ count and independent residual
counts of means $h(a_j(x)-a_j(z))^+$ and $h(a_j(z)-a_j(x))^+$ for the fine
and coarse paths, as in
[[lem-shared-minimum-poisson-count-coupling]]. Use independent copies across
channels and fresh copies on the two half intervals. Update the fine state after each half interval, and keep
the coarse propensities frozen at its state at the start of the coarse
interval. Then, for every bounded $g:\mathbb Z^d\to\mathbb R$,
$$\operatorname{Var}\!\left(g(Y_{h_\ell}(T))-g(Y_{h_{\ell-1}}(T))\right) \le C h_\ell,$$
where $C$ depends on $T$, the finite network, and $\|g\|_\infty$, but not
on $\ell$. This is a variance bound for the stated coupled Poisson leap;
independent levels are not covered.
alg-critical-reaction-binomial-guarded-t:
## Definition

**Inputs.** A finite state reaction system
[[def-reaction-network-propensity-system-and-generator]] with nonzero jump
vectors, initial state $x_0\in E$, horizon $T>0$, maximum leap
$\tau_{\max}>0$, critical threshold $n_c\in\mathbb N$, finite step budget
$B$ that is a nonnegative integer, and the ideal random draws required by
the procedure. For a state $x$ and channel $j$, define its admissible firing
capacity
$$\mathbb N_0:=\{0,1,2,\ldots\},\qquad m_j(x):=\max\{m\in\mathbb N_0:x+r\nu_j\in E \text{ for every integer }r\in\{0,\ldots,m\}\}.$$
Finiteness of $E$ and $\nu_j\ne0$ make this maximum finite. Let
$C(x)=\{j:m_j(x)\le n_c\}$ be the critical set. At each outer state $x$, hold
$C(x)$ fixed and form the finite reaction system on $E$ using only those
channels, with their original propensities. The critical SSA subroutine runs
the direct Gillespie method on this restricted system with event budget one
and horizon $\tau$; it returns its first event $(s,j_*)$ if it occurs by
$\tau$, and otherwise returns no event. The restricted system remains
admissible because its positive-rate transitions are among those of the
original system. The exactness theorem
[[thm-finite-state-gillespie-and-next-reaction-exactness]] applies under
Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, which are assumed for this subroutine.
That theorem's full-path law implies the one-event prefix law used here; the
finite event budget returns this first-event prefix only.

**Procedure.** Set $t=0$, $x=x_0$, and status **completed**.

1. If $t=T$, return the completed path. If $x\notin E$, return the current
   path prefix with status **invalid-state**. If the step budget is exhausted
   before $T$, return the current path prefix with status **inconclusive**.
   If $\lambda(x)=0$, hold $x$ fixed through $T$ and return **absorbed**.
2. Compute $C(x)$ and
   $$\tau=\min\!\left(T-t,\tau_{\max}, \min_{\substack{j\notin C(x)\\a_j(x)>0}}\frac{m_j(x)}{a_j(x)}\right),$$
   where the inner minimum over an empty set is $+\infty$. If $\tau\le0$,
   return **step-size-infeasible** with the current path prefix. Call
   critical SSA for horizon $\tau$. It returns either no critical event
   before $\tau$, or a pair $(s,j_*)$ with $0<s\le\tau$ and $j_*\in C(x)$.
   Set $\delta$ to $s$ in the event case and to $\tau$ otherwise.
3. Starting from $\widetilde x=x$, process each noncritical channel in a
   fixed order. Recompute $m_j(\widetilde x)$. If $a_j(\widetilde x)>0$ and
   $m_j(\widetilde x)=0$, return **critical-interface-required** with the
   current path prefix. Otherwise
   set $K_j=0$ when $m_j(\widetilde x)=0=a_j(\widetilde x)$. When
   $m_j(\widetilde x)>0$, set
   $p_j=a_j(\widetilde x)\delta/m_j(\widetilde x)$; if $p_j>1$, return
   **step-size-infeasible** with the current path prefix and without rejecting
   and resampling. Draw
   $K_j\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m_j,p_j)$ and update
   $\widetilde x\leftarrow\widetilde x+K_j\nu_j$.
4. If critical SSA returned $(s,j_*)$ but
   $\widetilde x+\nu_{j_*}\notin E$, return **inconclusive** with the current
   path prefix. Otherwise apply
   that one critical reaction. Set $x\leftarrow\widetilde x$ (after the
   critical reaction, if present), set $t\leftarrow t+\delta$, increase the
   step count, and repeat.

At every binomial update, $K_j\le m_j(\widetilde x)$, so each sequential
intermediate state stays in $E$. The finite budget prevents an infinite run.
Each loop processes at most $R$ noncritical channels and one first-event SSA
call over at most $R$ channels, so under a unit-operation convention its
work is $O(BR)$; random-number generation internals are excluded.
The direct-method random stream uses Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
through [[thm-countable-product-of-probability-spaces]]; the exact event law
uses them as stated in the cited exactness theorem.
This guarded procedure changes the Poisson count law: the binomial variance is
$m_jp_j(1-p_j)$, not the Poisson variance $a_j\delta$. The weak-order and MLMC
claims for explicit Poisson tau-leaping below do not transfer to this algorithm.
No correctness or convergence theorem for the guarded hybrid is claimed here.
lem-bounded-rate-reaction-generator-dynk:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $D$ and $F$ be disjoint
finite sets of states, and let a finite-channel reaction chain move from a
state $x\in D$ by channel $j$ to $x+\nu_j\in D\cup F$ at rate $a_j(x)$.
Assume its total rate is at most $A<\infty$ on $D$, and make every state in
$F$ absorbing. Let $v:[0,T]\times(D\cup F)\to\mathbb R$ have a continuously
differentiable time section for each state, with $\partial_t v$ continuous
in time. Define
$$Qf(x)=\sum_j a_j(x)(f(x+\nu_j)-f(x))\quad(x\in D),\qquad Qf(x)=0\quad(x\in F).$$
Then, for the stopped chain $X$ and $0\le t\le T$,
$$\mathbb E[v(t,X_t)] = \mathbb E[v(0,X_0)] + \mathbb E\int_0^t(\partial_s v(s,X_s)+Qv(s,\cdot)(X_s))\,ds.$$
In particular, $D$ may be the finite set of lattice states inside a compact
stopping region, and $F$ the finite set of one-jump exit destinations.
lem-poisson-tau-leap-one-step-weak-defec:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $E$ be finite, let
$A=\max_{x\in E}\sum_j a_j(x)$, and assume
$a_j(x)=0$ whenever $x+\nu_j\notin E$. Extend every state outside $E$ as
absorbing, as in [[alg-explicit-poisson-tau-leaping]]. For $h\ge0$, let
$Q_h$ be the exact reaction-chain transition kernel and $K_h$ the Poisson
tau-leap transition kernel. If $g:\mathbb Z^d\to\mathbb R$ is bounded, then
$$\left|(K_hg)(x)-g(x)-h(Qg)(x)\right| \le2A^2h^2\|g\|_\infty,$$
$$\left|(Q_hg)(x)-g(x)-h(Qg)(x)\right| \le2A^2h^2\|g\|_\infty,$$
and hence
$$\|K_hg-Q_hg\|_\infty\le4A^2h^2\|g\|_\infty.$$
The bounds include the multi-reaction leap probability that can trigger the
invalid-state branch.
thm-density-scaled-chemical-langevin-mod:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Use the density-scaled generators in
[[def-density-scaled-jump-and-chemical-langevin-generators]]. Let $K\subset U$
be compact and the closure of a bounded open stopping region with nonempty interior, let
$x_0\in\operatorname{int}K$, and let
$\mathcal L_V=x_0+\frac1V\mathbb Z^d$ be a containing lattice. For fixed $V$,
the set $D=\operatorname{int}K\cap\mathcal L_V$ is finite: boundedness of
$K$ bounds each integer coordinate index in the lattice. Let $X^V$ be the
jump process stopped at
$\tau_X=\inf\{t\ge0:X^V_t\notin\operatorname{int}K\}$ and let $Z^V$ be a
chemical Langevin diffusion stopped at
$\tau_Z=\inf\{t\ge0:Z^V_t\notin\operatorname{int}K\}$. Assume both stopped
processes exist, and write $\bar X_t=X^V_{t\wedge\tau_X}$ and
$\bar Z_t=Z^V_{t\wedge\tau_Z}$.

Assume $a_j\in C^3(U)$, $0\le a_j\le A_j$ on $K$, and every segment
$[x,x+\nu_j/V]$ for $x\in D$ with $a_j(x)>0$ lies in $U$. For a bounded
payoff $g$ with $|g|\le G$, suppose the stopped CLE backward solution
$$u(s,x)=\mathbb E_x[g(Z^V_{(T-s)\wedge\tau_Z})]$$
has an extension to an open neighborhood of $K$ and all these jump segments
that is $C^3$ in space and $C^1$ in time,
with $u(T,y)=g(y)$ on all states reached by the stopped jump chain and
$u(s,y)=g(y)$ on every exit state (including diffusion boundary points), and
$$\partial_su+\mathcal G_Vu=0\quad\text{on }[0,T]\times\operatorname{int}K, \qquad \|D^3u(s,y)\|\le M,$$
and $\partial_su$ is continuous in time on the stated neighborhood. The
third-derivative bound holds along every jump segment. The derivatives are
spatial Fréchet derivatives with operator norm. Then
$$\left|\mathbb E g(\bar X_T)-\mathbb E g(\bar Z_T)\right| \le \frac{TM}{6V^2}\sum_{j=1}^R A_j\|\nu_j\|^3.$$
If the original local jump and diffusion models are defined through $T$ and
are coupled to agree with their stopped versions up to their respective
exits, then
$$\left|\mathbb E g(X^V_T)-\mathbb E g(Z^V_T)\right| \le \frac{TM}{6V^2}\sum_{j=1}^R A_j\|\nu_j\|^3 +2G\bigl(\mathbb P(\tau_X\le T)+\mathbb P(\tau_Z\le T)\bigr).$$
The $V^{-2}$ term is density-model error from the generator expansion; the
exit term is separate. Neither term is time-discretization error. The
existence and regularity of the CLE backward solution are assumptions, not
consequences of this estimate.
thm-poisson-tau-leap-weak-order-one-with:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let
$E\subseteq\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^d$ be finite, let
$A=\max_{x\in E}\sum_j a_j(x)<\infty$ for the system
[[def-reaction-network-propensity-system-and-generator]], and assume
$a_j(x)=0$ whenever $x+\nu_j\notin E$. Extend the exact chain by making every
state outside $E$ absorbing, and let $K_h$ be the tau-leap kernel in
[[alg-explicit-poisson-tau-leaping]] with the same absorbing-invalid-state
convention. For $T=Nh$ with $N\in\mathbb N$, an initial state $x_0\in E$, and
a bounded payoff $g:\mathbb Z^d\to\mathbb R$, the leap satisfies
$$\left|\mathbb E_{x_0}g(Y_N)-\mathbb E_{x_0}g(X_T)\right| \le4A^2T h\,\|g\|_\infty.$$
Its probability of ever entering an invalid state by $T$ is at most
$\tfrac12A^2T h$. This separately bounds the absorbing invalid-state branch;
the result makes no claim for unbounded rates.
cor-mlmc-complexity-for-poisson-tau-leap:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, and the finite-state hypotheses of
[[thm-poisson-tau-leap-weak-order-one-with-exit-bound]] and
[[thm-minimum-intensity-tau-leap-level-variance]], with bounded payoff $g$.
Use levels $h_\ell=T2^{-\ell}$ and couple adjacent Poisson tau-leap paths by
the shared-minimum construction. Under the work convention that each channel
Poisson draw, propensity evaluation, and stoichiometric update has unit cost,
for each $\ell\ge1$ one correction sample costs at most $C h_\ell^{-1}$:
there are $T/h_\ell$ fine steps and $T/h_{\ell-1}$ coarse steps, with $R$
draws per step. The base-level sample uses one path and costs $O(R)$, which
is $O(h_0^{-1})$ for fixed $T$. The level bias is $O(h_L)$ and the
correction variance is $O(h_\ell)$. Therefore, for all
sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$, deterministic sample counts in the generic
multilevel estimator can achieve mean square error at most $\epsilon^2$ with
work
$$O\!\left(\epsilon^{-2}(\log\epsilon^{-1})^2\right).$$
This conclusion applies only to the explicit Poisson leap and the bounded
finite-state hypotheses above. It is not a correctness or error guarantee
for the guarded binomial algorithm
[[alg-critical-reaction-binomial-guarded-tau-leaping]].
